# Overview

This notebook executes the confirmatory and primary quantitative analyses for Study 1 as specified in the preregistration. It runs end-to-end from raw CSVs in `data/raw/` through composite scoring, exclusions, the ten coequal confirmatory tests with BH-FDR correction, the verbosity-adjusted parallel analysis, behavioral DVs, the legal-expertise directional hypothesis, item-level analyses with forest plots, and exploratory moderators and mediation. Outputs include `data/processed/analytic_data.csv` and `data/processed/composite_scores.csv` for use by the NLP and integration notebooks.

The notebook is structured to mirror the preregistration sections (7 → 8 → 9.1–9.9). Each major analysis section produces tables and figures that are written to `outputs/R/`.

## 1.2 Helper functions

```{r helpers}
# Welch's t with Hedges' g (effectsize::hedges_g), 95% CI, BF10, Mann-Whitney U  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-G)
welch_full <- function(data, dv, group_var = "condition_label",
                       ref_level = "LowA", comp_level = "HighA",
                       paired = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided") {
  d <- data %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[dv]]), !is.na(.data[[group_var]]))
  ref <- d[[dv]][d[[group_var]] == ref_level]
  comp <- d[[dv]][d[[group_var]] == comp_level]

  if (length(ref) < 3 || length(comp) < 3) {
    return(tibble(
      dv = dv, n_ref = length(ref), n_comp = length(comp),
      mean_ref = NA_real_, sd_ref = NA_real_,
      mean_comp = NA_real_, sd_comp = NA_real_,
      t = NA_real_, df = NA_real_, p = NA_real_,
      d = NA_real_, d_lo = NA_real_, d_hi = NA_real_,
      bf10 = NA_real_, U = NA_real_, p_mw = NA_real_, r_mw = NA_real_
    ))
  }

  tt <- t.test(comp, ref, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = alternative)
  dd <- effectsize::hedges_g(comp, ref, paired = FALSE, ci = 0.95)

  bf <- tryCatch({
    bf_obj <- BayesFactor::ttestBF(x = comp, y = ref, paired = FALSE,
                                    rscale = 0.707, nullInterval = NULL)
    as.numeric(BayesFactor::extractBF(bf_obj)$bf)[1]
  }, error = function(e) NA_real_)

  mw <- tryCatch({
    suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(comp, ref, alternative = alternative,
                                  exact = FALSE, correct = TRUE))
  }, error = function(e) NULL)

  if (!is.null(mw)) {
    n_total <- length(ref) + length(comp)
    z_approx <- qnorm(mw$p.value / 2, lower.tail = FALSE) * sign(median(comp) - median(ref))
    r_mw <- abs(z_approx) / sqrt(n_total)
  } else {
    r_mw <- NA_real_
  }

  tibble(
    dv = dv,
    n_ref = length(ref), n_comp = length(comp),
    mean_ref = mean(ref, na.rm = TRUE), sd_ref = sd(ref, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_comp = mean(comp, na.rm = TRUE), sd_comp = sd(comp, na.rm = TRUE),
    t = unname(tt$statistic), df = unname(tt$parameter), p = tt$p.value,
    d = dd$Hedges_g, d_lo = dd$CI_low, d_hi = dd$CI_high,
    bf10 = bf,
    U = if (!is.null(mw)) unname(mw$statistic) else NA_real_,
    p_mw = if (!is.null(mw)) mw$p.value else NA_real_,
    r_mw = r_mw
  )
}

# Reverse-score helper: x is on a scale of 1..max
rev_score <- function(x, max_val) max_val + 1 - x

# Format p-values for tables
fmt_p <- function(p) {
  ifelse(is.na(p), "—",
    ifelse(p < 0.001, "<.001",
      ifelse(p < 0.01, sprintf("%.3f", p),
        sprintf("%.3f", p))))
}

# Format Bayes factors
fmt_bf <- function(bf) {
  ifelse(is.na(bf), "—",
    ifelse(bf >= 100, sprintf("%.0f", bf),
      ifelse(bf >= 10, sprintf("%.1f", bf),
        ifelse(bf >= 1, sprintf("%.2f", bf),
          sprintf("1/%.1f", 1/bf)))))
}

# BF10 verbal interpretation (Jeffreys-Lee)
bf_verbal <- function(bf) {
  case_when(
    is.na(bf) ~ "—",
    bf > 100 ~ "Extreme H1",
    bf > 30 ~ "Very strong H1",
    bf > 10 ~ "Strong H1",
    bf > 3 ~ "Moderate H1",
    bf > 1 ~ "Anecdotal H1",
    bf > 1/3 ~ "Anecdotal H0",
    bf > 1/10 ~ "Moderate H0",
    bf > 1/30 ~ "Strong H0",
    TRUE ~ "Very strong H0"
  )
}

# Tidy a regression for table output
tidy_lm <- function(m) {
  broom::tidy(m, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 4)))
}

# Save tables and figures
save_table <- function(tbl, name, ...) {
  readr::write_csv(tbl, here("outputs", "R", "tables", paste0(name, ".csv")))
  invisible(tbl)
}
save_fig <- function(p, name, w = 8, h = 5) {
  ggplot2::ggsave(here("outputs", "R", "figures", paste0(name, ".png")),
                  plot = p, width = w, height = h, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
  ggplot2::ggsave(here("outputs", "R", "figures", paste0(name, ".pdf")),
                  plot = p, width = w, height = h)
  invisible(p)
}
```

# 2. Load raw data

The raw CSVs are one row per participant, one file per session. Column counts vary across files because per-message columns expand with conversation length. We read with `bind_rows()` which tolerates this — short conversations get NA for unused message columns.

```{r load-raw}
raw_dir <- here("data", "raw")
raw_files <- list.files(raw_dir, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)

cat(glue("Found {length(raw_files)} raw CSV files in {raw_dir}\n"))

raw <- raw_files %>%
  map_dfr(~suppressMessages(readr::read_csv(.x, show_col_types = FALSE,
                                             progress = FALSE)) %>%
            mutate(across(everything(), as.character))) %>%
  type_convert(guess_integer = TRUE)

cat(glue("\nLoaded {nrow(raw)} sessions × {ncol(raw)} columns\n"))
cat(glue("Conditions in raw data: HighA = {sum(raw$condition_label == 'HighA', na.rm = TRUE)}, ",
        "LowA = {sum(raw$condition_label == 'LowA', na.rm = TRUE)}\n"))
```

# 3. Exclusions (Prereg §7)

The preregistration specifies five participant-level exclusion criteria, plus pilot/test session and duplicate handling. Implementation follows Section 7 verbatim.

## 3.1 Apply exclusion criteria

```{r exclusions}
# Pre-specified pilot/test SONA IDs (Prereg §7.2)
pilot_ids <- c("TEST", "<PILOT_ID_1>", "<PILOT_ID_2>")  # pilot and lab-member test IDs are withheld from the public copy (shared with the data under a data use agreement)

# Build exclusion flags
ex <- raw %>%
  mutate(
    sona_id = as.character(sona_id),
    # 7.1.1 attention failure both passes
    excl_attention = (attn1_pass == FALSE) & (attn1_retry_pass == FALSE) &
                      !is.na(attn1_pass) & !is.na(attn1_retry_pass),
    # 7.1.2 comprehension
    excl_comprehension = (comprehension_correct == FALSE) & !is.na(comprehension_correct),
    # 7.1.3 captcha
    excl_captcha = (captcha_pass == FALSE) & !is.na(captcha_pass),
    # 7.1.4 self-reported AI use (1 = Yes)
    excl_ai_used = (d_ai_used_in_study == 1) & !is.na(d_ai_used_in_study),
    # 7.1.5 self-reported non-serious (1 = No, did not complete seriously)
    excl_not_serious = (d_serious == 1) & !is.na(d_serious),
    # 7.2 pilot/test sessions
    excl_pilot = sona_id %in% pilot_ids
  )

# 7.3 Duplicate SONA: keep earliest by start_time
ex <- ex %>%
  arrange(sona_id, start_time) %>%
  group_by(sona_id) %>%
  mutate(
    session_rank = row_number(),
    excl_duplicate = (session_rank > 1) & !is.na(sona_id) & sona_id != ""
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Combine all exclusions
ex <- ex %>%
  mutate(
    excl_any = excl_attention | excl_comprehension | excl_captcha |
               excl_ai_used | excl_not_serious | excl_pilot | excl_duplicate
  )

# CONSORT-style flow
flow <- tibble(
  Step = c(
    "Sessions in raw data",
    "Excluded: pilot/test SONA",
    "Excluded: duplicate session (kept earliest)",
    "Excluded: failed attention check (both attempts)",
    "Excluded: failed comprehension check",
    "Excluded: failed CAPTCHA",
    "Excluded: self-reported AI tool use",
    "Excluded: self-reported non-serious responding",
    "Final analytic sample (primary)"
  ),
  N = c(
    nrow(ex),
    sum(ex$excl_pilot),
    sum(ex$excl_duplicate),
    sum(ex$excl_attention & !ex$excl_pilot & !ex$excl_duplicate),
    sum(ex$excl_comprehension & !ex$excl_pilot & !ex$excl_duplicate & !ex$excl_attention),
    sum(ex$excl_captcha & !ex$excl_pilot & !ex$excl_duplicate &
        !ex$excl_attention & !ex$excl_comprehension),
    sum(ex$excl_ai_used & !ex$excl_pilot & !ex$excl_duplicate &
        !ex$excl_attention & !ex$excl_comprehension & !ex$excl_captcha),
    sum(ex$excl_not_serious & !ex$excl_pilot & !ex$excl_duplicate &
        !ex$excl_attention & !ex$excl_comprehension & !ex$excl_captcha & !ex$excl_ai_used),
    sum(!ex$excl_any)
  )
)

flow %>%
  kbl(caption = "CONSORT exclusion flow", booktabs = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(1, bold = TRUE) %>%
  row_spec(nrow(flow), bold = TRUE, background = "#F0F8FF")

save_table(flow, "01_exclusion_flow")
```

## 3.2 Build the two analysis samples

Per Prereg §7.7, all primary analyses run on both the strict-exclusion sample and a sensitivity sample (only pilot/test and duplicate exclusions applied).

```{r build-samples}
df_primary <- ex %>% filter(!excl_any)
df_sensitivity <- ex %>% filter(!excl_pilot & !excl_duplicate)

cat(glue("Primary sample N = {nrow(df_primary)} (HighA = {sum(df_primary$condition_label == 'HighA')}, ",
        "LowA = {sum(df_primary$condition_label == 'LowA')})\n"))
cat(glue("Sensitivity sample N = {nrow(df_sensitivity)} (HighA = {sum(df_sensitivity$condition_label == 'HighA')}, ",
        "LowA = {sum(df_sensitivity$condition_label == 'LowA')})\n"))

# Set condition_label as a factor with LowA reference
df_primary <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(condition_label = factor(condition_label, levels = c("LowA", "HighA")))
df_sensitivity <- df_sensitivity %>%
  mutate(condition_label = factor(condition_label, levels = c("LowA", "HighA")))
```

# 4. Composite scoring (Prereg §6)

```{r composites}
score_composites <- function(d) {
  d %>%
    mutate(
      # TIPI-Self (7-point, reverse-score using 8-x)
      tipi_self_extra = (tipi_self_1 + (8 - tipi_self_6)) / 2,
      tipi_self_agree = ((8 - tipi_self_2) + tipi_self_7) / 2,
      tipi_self_consc = (tipi_self_3 + (8 - tipi_self_8)) / 2,
      tipi_self_emostab = ((8 - tipi_self_4) + tipi_self_9) / 2,
      tipi_self_open = (tipi_self_5 + (8 - tipi_self_10)) / 2,

      # TIPI-Bot (7-point, same scoring)
      tipi_bot_extra = (tipi_bot_1 + (8 - tipi_bot_6)) / 2,
      tipi_bot_agree = ((8 - tipi_bot_2) + tipi_bot_7) / 2,
      tipi_bot_consc = (tipi_bot_3 + (8 - tipi_bot_8)) / 2,
      tipi_bot_emostab = ((8 - tipi_bot_4) + tipi_bot_9) / 2,
      tipi_bot_open = (tipi_bot_5 + (8 - tipi_bot_10)) / 2,

      # Manipulation check single items
      # NOTE: mc_neuroticism item ("How emotionally stable or unstable was Sylva?")
      # is bipolar phrasing on a unipolar 1-5 scale and is structurally ambiguous.
      # We retain the raw value for disclosure but DO NOT score a derived emostab
      # composite (no mc_emostab_score). The multi-item TIPI-Bot Emotional Stability
      # is the canonical check for that trait. See §5.3 methodological note.
      mc_extraversion_score = mc_extraversion,
      mc_agreeableness_score = mc_agreeableness,

      # PSR composite + subscales
      psr_connection = rowMeans(across(c(psr_1, psr_2, psr_3, psr_4)), na.rm = FALSE),
      psr_desire     = rowMeans(across(c(psr_5, psr_6, psr_7, psr_8)), na.rm = FALSE),
      psr_caring     = rowMeans(across(c(psr_9, psr_10, psr_11, psr_12)), na.rm = FALSE),
      psr_total      = rowMeans(across(starts_with("psr_") & matches("^psr_\\d+$")), na.rm = FALSE),

      # EC, Trust, ET, MA, MP composites
      ec_total    = rowMeans(across(starts_with("ec_") & matches("^ec_\\d+$")), na.rm = FALSE),
      trust_total = rowMeans(across(starts_with("tr_") & matches("^tr_\\d+$")), na.rm = FALSE),
      et_total    = rowMeans(across(starts_with("et_") & matches("^et_\\d+$")), na.rm = FALSE),
      ma_total    = rowMeans(across(starts_with("ma_") & matches("^ma_\\d+$")), na.rm = FALSE),
      mp_total    = rowMeans(across(starts_with("mp_") & matches("^mp_\\d+$")), na.rm = FALSE),

      # Liability components
      liab_corp   = rowMeans(across(c(liab_1, liab_2, liab_3, liab_4, liab_5)), na.rm = FALSE),
      liab_chat   = rowMeans(across(c(liab_6, liab_7, liab_8)), na.rm = FALSE),
      liab_user   = rowMeans(across(c(liab_9, liab_10)), na.rm = FALSE),
      liab_harm   = rowMeans(across(c(liab_11, liab_12)), na.rm = FALSE),

      # PHQ-4 (0-3 scale)
      phq4_anx    = phq4_1 + phq4_2,
      phq4_dep    = phq4_3 + phq4_4,
      phq4_total  = phq4_1 + phq4_2 + phq4_3 + phq4_4,

      # GAAIS (item 10 reverse-scored in positive subscale; items 19, 20 reverse-scored in negative subscale)
      gaais_pos = (gaais_1 + gaais_2 + gaais_3 + gaais_4 + gaais_5 +
                   gaais_6 + gaais_7 + gaais_8 + gaais_9 + (6 - gaais_10)) / 10,
      gaais_neg = (gaais_11 + gaais_12 + gaais_13 + gaais_14 + gaais_15 +
                   gaais_16 + gaais_17 + gaais_18 + (6 - gaais_19) + (6 - gaais_20)) / 10
    )
}

df_primary <- score_composites(df_primary)
df_sensitivity <- score_composites(df_sensitivity)

# Quick sanity check on composites
df_primary %>%
  select(condition_label, tipi_bot_agree, mc_agreeableness_score,
         psr_total, ec_total, trust_total, et_total,
         ma_total, mp_total, liab_corp, liab_chat, liab_user, liab_harm) %>%
  pivot_longer(-condition_label, names_to = "Composite", values_to = "Score") %>%
  group_by(condition_label, Composite) %>%
  summarize(M = mean(Score, na.rm = TRUE), SD = sd(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = sum(!is.na(Score)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition_label, values_from = c(M, SD, n)) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Composite descriptives by condition (primary sample)",
      booktabs = TRUE, digits = 2) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

# 5. Manipulation Integrity (Prereg §8.1)

## 5.1 Primary manipulation check: TIPI-Bot Agreeableness

```{r mc-tipi-A}
mc_tipi_A <- welch_full(df_primary, "tipi_bot_agree")
mc_tipi_A %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3))) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Manipulation check: TIPI-Bot Agreeableness (primary)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

cat("Hedges' g =", round(mc_tipi_A$d, 2),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-G)
    "[95% CI: ", round(mc_tipi_A$d_lo, 2), ", ", round(mc_tipi_A$d_hi, 2), "]\n")
cat("BF10 =", fmt_bf(mc_tipi_A$bf10), " (", bf_verbal(mc_tipi_A$bf10), ")\n")
```

## 5.2 Secondary single-item check: warmth/support

```{r mc-singleitem}
mc_single <- welch_full(df_primary, "mc_agreeableness_score")
mc_single %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3))) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Single-item manipulation check (warmth/support)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## 5.3 Diffusion checks (held-constant traits)

These should *not* differ between conditions — MOD_HIGH_E and MOD_LOW_N blocks are identical across conditions. Bonferroni correction is applied across the *three* psychometrically-clean diffusion tests (α = .0167 per test).

**Methodological note on the dropped `mc_neuroticism` item:** The single-item check for emotional stability used the prompt *"How emotionally stable or unstable was Sylva?"* on a 1–5 unipolar response scale (1 = "Not at all", 5 = "Extremely"). This is a bipolar question paired with a unipolar scale, which is structurally ambiguous: a participant who perceives Sylva as very stable could legitimately answer "5 = Extremely [stable]" or "1 = Not at all [unstable]" — both readings are coherent. Because the two readings produce opposite numeric responses to the same underlying perception, the item cannot be coherently scored. At the interim looks on which this decision was made (between N = 80 and N = 96), it ran in the *opposite* direction from the two-item TIPI-Bot Emotional Stability scale, which is the psychometric symptom of an item that participants interpret two ways. In the final analytic sample the HighA − LowA effect is *g* = `r sprintf("%.2f", welch_full(df_primary, "mc_neuroticism")$d)` on the raw item versus *g* = `r sprintf("%.2f", welch_full(df_primary, "tipi_bot_emostab")$d)` on TIPI-Bot Emotional Stability. <!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (C5): interim history labelled as such, final-sample values added live; "four-item" corrected to "two-item" (TIPI emotional stability = items 4 and 9) --> We exclude `mc_neuroticism` from all analyses and report only the multi-item TIPI-Bot Emotional Stability scale as the diffusion check for that trait. The item will be reworded for Studies 1b–1d to a unipolar form (e.g., *"How emotionally stable did Sylva seem?"*, anchored 1=Not at all stable to 5=Extremely stable).

```{r diffusion}
# Three psychometrically-clean diffusion tests (Bonferroni alpha = .0167)
# mc_neuroticism (and its derived mc_emostab_score) is excluded — see methodological note above
diffusion_dvs <- c("tipi_bot_extra", "tipi_bot_emostab", "mc_extraversion_score")
diffusion_results <- map_dfr(diffusion_dvs, ~welch_full(df_primary, .x))
diffusion_results <- diffusion_results %>%
  mutate(p_bonf = pmin(p * 3, 1),
         significant_at_corrected = p_bonf < 0.05,
         flag = ifelse(significant_at_corrected, "⚠ DIFFUSION", "OK"))

diffusion_results %>%
  select(dv, mean_ref, sd_ref, mean_comp, sd_comp, t, df, p, p_bonf, d, d_lo, d_hi, bf10, flag) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)),
         bf10 = fmt_bf(bf10)) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Diffusion checks on held-constant traits (Bonferroni-corrected, three tests)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

save_table(diffusion_results, "02_diffusion_checks")
```


```{r mc-figure, fig.height=4}
  scale_color_manual(values = cond_colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Manipulation Check: TIPI-Bot Agreeableness",
       subtitle = glue("Hedges' g = {round(mc_tipi_A$d, 2)} [95% CI: {round(mc_tipi_A$d_lo, 2)}, {round(mc_tipi_A$d_hi, 2)}]"),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-G)
       x = NULL, y = "TIPI-Bot Agreeableness (1–7)") +
  ylim(1, 7)

p_mc
save_fig(p_mc, "01_manipulation_check_tipiA", w = 6, h = 4.5)
```

# 6. Ten Coequal Confirmatory Tests with BH-FDR (Prereg §8.2)

The ten DV composites are tested under an identical statistical template: Welch's *t*, Hedges' *g* with 95% CI, BF₁₀, Mann-Whitney *U* as non-parametric robustness check. The ten *p*-values are submitted to the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure with *q* = .05. <!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-G): label was "Cohen's d ... (Hedges correction)"; the statistic is effectsize::hedges_g -->

## 6.1 Run the ten confirmatory tests

```{r ten-confirmatory}
confirmatory_dvs <- c(
  "psr_total", "ec_total", "trust_total", "et_total",
  "ma_total", "mp_total",
  "liab_corp", "liab_chat", "liab_user", "liab_harm"
)

dv_labels <- c(
  psr_total = "Parasocial Relationship",
  ec_total = "Emotional Connection",
  trust_total = "Trust",
  et_total = "Experience-Taking",
  ma_total = "Moral Agency",
  mp_total = "Moral Patiency",
  liab_corp = "Corporate Liability",
  liab_chat = "Chatbot Responsibility",
  liab_user = "User Responsibility",
  liab_harm = "Harm Severity"
)

# Primary sample
results_primary <- map_dfr(confirmatory_dvs, ~welch_full(df_primary, .x)) %>%
  mutate(
    dv_label = dv_labels[dv],
    q_bh = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
    p_mw_bh = p.adjust(p_mw, method = "BH"),
    bf_interp = bf_verbal(bf10),
    confirmed = (q_bh < 0.05) & (bf10 >= 3),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C4): stated rule is BF10 >= 3 (was > 3)
    partially_supported = ((q_bh < 0.05) & !(bf10 >= 3)) | (!(q_bh < 0.05) & (bf10 >= 3)),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C4): complement uses BF10 >= 3
    interpretation = case_when(
      confirmed ~ "Confirmed",
      partially_supported ~ "Partial",
      TRUE ~ "Inconclusive"
    )
  )

# Sensitivity sample (for the §7.7 comparison)
results_sensitivity <- map_dfr(confirmatory_dvs, ~welch_full(df_sensitivity, .x)) %>%
  mutate(
    dv_label = dv_labels[dv],
    q_bh = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
  )

results_primary %>%
  select(dv_label, n_ref, mean_ref, sd_ref, n_comp, mean_comp, sd_comp,
         t, df, p, q_bh, d, d_lo, d_hi, bf10, p_mw, interpretation) %>%
  mutate(across(c(mean_ref, sd_ref, mean_comp, sd_comp, t, df, d, d_lo, d_hi), ~round(., 2)),
         p = fmt_p(p), q_bh = fmt_p(q_bh), p_mw = fmt_p(p_mw),
         bf10 = fmt_bf(bf10)) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Ten coequal confirmatory tests (BH-FDR-corrected, primary sample)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE) %>%
  row_spec(which(results_primary$confirmed), background = "#E6F4EA")

save_table(results_primary, "03_confirmatory_primary")
save_table(results_sensitivity, "03_confirmatory_sensitivity")
```

## 6.4 Equivalence tests (Prereg §11.4)

For each of the ten confirmatory DVs we conduct a two-one-sided equivalence test (TOST; Lakens, 2017) with bounds at ±d = 0.40, the prereg-specified smallest effect size of interest. <!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (C3/C5): equivalence is now defined by the implemented decision rule (tost_p_max < .05); the previous wording defined it by the CI and called for a "non-rejected" equivalence test, which is backwards. -->
A DV is classified as "equivalent" to zero when the TOST is significant: both one-sided tests against ±0.40 reject at p < .05 (`tost_p_max < .05`). The Hedges's g(av) 90% CI reported in `smd_lo90`/`smd_hi90` is descriptive; because TOSTER computes the TOST p-values and this CI by different methods, the CI can lie just inside ±0.40 while the TOST narrowly fails at the boundary (or vice versa). Any such DV is listed by the `[C3 diagnostic]` output below and flagged in the `ci90_within_bounds` column of `04b_tost_equivalence.csv`; the classification always follows the TOST p-values. Equivalence-test results complement Bayes factors: a DV with BF10 < 1/3 AND a significant equivalence test (TOST p < .05) together provide the strongest evidence for the null available here. A DV with BF10 < 1/3 whose TOST is not significant at .05 is characterized as "absence of evidence" rather than "evidence of absence." <!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (C3/C5) -->

```{r tost-equivalence}
tost_results <- map_dfr(confirmatory_dvs, function(dv) {
  d_sub <- df_primary %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[dv]]))
  ref  <- d_sub[[dv]][d_sub$condition_label == "LowA"]
  comp <- d_sub[[dv]][d_sub$condition_label == "HighA"]
  if (length(ref) < 5 || length(comp) < 5) return(NULL)

  tost_obj <- tryCatch(
    TOSTER::tsum_TOST(
      m1 = mean(comp, na.rm = TRUE), sd1 = sd(comp, na.rm = TRUE), n1 = length(comp),
      m2 = mean(ref,  na.rm = TRUE), sd2 = sd(ref,  na.rm = TRUE), n2 = length(ref),
      low_eqbound = -0.40, high_eqbound = 0.40, eqbound_type = "SMD",
      alpha = 0.05
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(tost_obj)) return(NULL)

  # Pull the two one-sided p-values; equivalence is concluded when BOTH one-sided nulls are rejected at p < .05  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3/C5): comment said "equivalence is rejected", which is backwards
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(tost_obj$TOST)[2:3], c("TOST Lower", "TOST Upper")))  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): guard positional p-value rows
  tost_lower_p <- tost_obj$TOST$p.value[2]   # H0: true d ≤ -0.40 (reject -> bounded above lower)
  tost_upper_p <- tost_obj$TOST$p.value[3]   # H0: true d ≥ +0.40 (reject -> bounded below upper)
  tost_p_max   <- max(tost_lower_p, tost_upper_p, na.rm = TRUE)
  equivalent   <- tost_p_max < 0.05

  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): tost_obj$effsize has two rows, "Raw" (mean difference) and the
  # standardized row (TOSTER 0.8.6 labels it "Hedges's g(av)" for Welch). Row [1] is the RAW  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3)
  # difference, which was previously stored as `smd`. Select both rows BY NAME.  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3)
  es_tab   <- tost_obj$effsize                                        # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): effect-size table
  smd_name <- setdiff(rownames(es_tab), "Raw")                        # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): standardized row name
  stopifnot("Raw" %in% rownames(es_tab), length(smd_name) == 1,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3)
            grepl("Hedges|Cohen|Glass", smd_name))                    # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): assert expected rows
  es_raw <- es_tab["Raw", , drop = FALSE]                             # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): raw mean-difference row
  es_smd <- es_tab[smd_name, , drop = FALSE]                          # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): standardized (SMD) row

  tibble(
    dv = dv,
    dv_label = unname(dv_labels[dv]),
    n_lowA = length(ref), n_highA = length(comp),
    smd = es_smd$estimate,        # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): standardized estimate (was raw row [1])
    smd_lo90 = es_smd$lower.ci,   # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): standardized 90% CI lower (was raw row [1])
    smd_hi90 = es_smd$upper.ci,   # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): standardized 90% CI upper (was raw row [1])
    tost_p_lower = tost_lower_p,
    tost_p_upper = tost_upper_p,
    tost_p_max   = tost_p_max,
    equivalent   = equivalent,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3)
    smd_type  = smd_name,           # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): added — which SMD TOSTER reports
    raw_diff  = es_raw$estimate,    # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): added — raw mean difference (HighA - LowA)
    raw_lo90  = es_raw$lower.ci,    # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): added — raw 90% CI lower
    raw_hi90  = es_raw$upper.ci,    # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): added — raw 90% CI upper
    ci90_within_bounds = (es_smd$lower.ci > -0.40) & (es_smd$upper.ci < 0.40)  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): added diagnostic
  )
})

# FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): diagnostic — print any DV where "SMD 90% CI inside ±0.40" disagrees with the
# TOST decision (TOST tests on the raw scale with SMD-converted bounds, so borderline cases can differ).  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3)
tost_ci_disagree <- tost_results %>% filter(ci90_within_bounds != equivalent)  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3): disagreement rows
if (nrow(tost_ci_disagree) > 0) {                                                # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3)
  cat("\n[C3 diagnostic] SMD 90% CI-within-bounds disagrees with the TOST decision for:\n")  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3)
  print(as.data.frame(tost_ci_disagree %>%  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3)
          select(dv_label, smd, smd_lo90, smd_hi90, tost_p_max, equivalent, ci90_within_bounds)))  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3)
} else {                                                                         # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3)
  cat("\n[C3 diagnostic] SMD 90% CI-within-bounds agrees with the TOST decision for all DVs.\n")  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3)
}                                                                                # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3)

tost_results %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)),
         across(matches("p_"), fmt_p),
         equivalent = ifelse(equivalent, "✓ equivalent", "✗ not equivalent")) %>%
  kbl(caption = "TOST equivalence tests on the ten confirmatory DVs (bounds ±d = 0.40)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE)

# Cross-classify with BF10 categories for the headline interpretation.
# IMPORTANT: compare the BOOLEAN `equivalent` column here (TRUE/FALSE), not the
# ✓/✗ string version, which doesn't exist until we re-format for display below.
# A previous version compared `equivalent == "✓ equivalent"` and silently
# returned all "—" because the boolean never matched the string.
tost_x_bf <- tost_results %>%
  left_join(results_primary %>% select(dv, bf10), by = "dv") %>%
  mutate(
    bf10_class = case_when(
      is.na(bf10) ~ "—",
      bf10 < 1/10 ~ "Strong/very-strong H0",
      bf10 < 1/3  ~ "Moderate H0",
      bf10 < 1    ~ "Anecdotal H0",
      bf10 < 3    ~ "Anecdotal H1",
      TRUE        ~ "Moderate+ H1"
    ),
    null_evidence = case_when(
      equivalent == TRUE  & !is.na(bf10) & bf10 < 1/3 ~ "Evidence of absence",
      equivalent == FALSE & !is.na(bf10) & bf10 < 1/3 ~ "Bayesian-only null",
      equivalent == TRUE  & !is.na(bf10) & bf10 >= 1/3 & bf10 < 3 ~ "TOST-only equivalence",
      equivalent == FALSE & !is.na(bf10) & bf10 >= 3 ~ "Evidence of presence",
      TRUE ~ "Inconclusive"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(dv_label, smd, smd_lo90, smd_hi90, tost_p_max, equivalent, bf10_class, null_evidence)

# Keep the boolean for downstream filtering, but make the display friendly
tost_x_bf_display <- tost_x_bf %>%
  mutate(equivalent = ifelse(equivalent, "✓ equivalent", "✗ not equivalent"))

tost_x_bf_display %>%
  kbl(caption = "Joint interpretation: TOST × Bayesian evidence categories") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE)

# Summary count for the manuscript
n_evidence_of_absence <- sum(tost_x_bf$null_evidence == "Evidence of absence", na.rm = TRUE)
n_evidence_of_presence <- sum(tost_x_bf$null_evidence == "Evidence of presence", na.rm = TRUE)
n_bayesian_only_null  <- sum(tost_x_bf$null_evidence == "Bayesian-only null", na.rm = TRUE)
n_inconclusive        <- sum(tost_x_bf$null_evidence == "Inconclusive", na.rm = TRUE)

cat(glue::glue(
  "\n--- Joint TOST × Bayesian classification ---\n",
  "Evidence of absence (TOST equivalent AND BF10 < 1/3): ",
  "{n_evidence_of_absence} of {nrow(tost_x_bf)} DVs.\n",
  "Evidence of presence (TOST not equivalent AND BF10 ≥ 3): ",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C4): label matches rule bf10 >= 3
  "{n_evidence_of_presence} of {nrow(tost_x_bf)} DVs.\n",
  "Bayesian-only null (BF10 < 1/3 but TOST not significant at .05): ",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C3/C5): label matches the implemented rule (was "CI too wide for equivalence")
  "{n_bayesian_only_null} of {nrow(tost_x_bf)} DVs.\n",
  "Inconclusive: {n_inconclusive} of {nrow(tost_x_bf)} DVs.\n"
))

# Name the DVs in each headline category
ev_absence_dvs <- tost_x_bf %>% filter(null_evidence == "Evidence of absence") %>% pull(dv_label)
ev_presence_dvs <- tost_x_bf %>% filter(null_evidence == "Evidence of presence") %>% pull(dv_label)

if (length(ev_absence_dvs) > 0) {
  cat(glue::glue(
    "\nDVs with evidence of absence: {paste(ev_absence_dvs, collapse = '; ')}\n"
  ))
}
if (length(ev_presence_dvs) > 0) {
  cat(glue::glue(
    "DVs with evidence of presence: {paste(ev_presence_dvs, collapse = '; ')}\n"
  ))
}

save_table(tost_results, "04b_tost_equivalence")
save_table(tost_x_bf,    "04c_tost_x_bayes_classification")
```

## 6.4.1 Equivalence robustness: raw-metric bounds (TOSTER author's recommendation)

The TOSTER package emits a warning when SMD bounds are used because the SMD pivot approximation can be biased; raw-metric bounds are recommended (Lakens, 2024). Our preregistration specified SMD bounds at ±0.40, which we keep as the primary equivalence test. As a robustness check we also compute equivalence with raw bounds set per DV at 0.40 × pooled SD; if both procedures agree on which DVs reach equivalence, the SMD bias is not material for our conclusions.

```{r tost-raw-robustness}
tost_raw_results <- map_dfr(confirmatory_dvs, function(dv) {
  d_sub <- df_primary %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[dv]]))
  ref  <- d_sub[[dv]][d_sub$condition_label == "LowA"]
  comp <- d_sub[[dv]][d_sub$condition_label == "HighA"]
  if (length(ref) < 5 || length(comp) < 5) return(NULL)

  # Pooled SD for raw-bound conversion
  n1 <- length(comp); n2 <- length(ref)
  pooled_sd <- sqrt(((n1 - 1) * var(comp, na.rm = TRUE) +
                     (n2 - 1) * var(ref,  na.rm = TRUE)) / (n1 + n2 - 2))
  raw_bound <- 0.40 * pooled_sd

  tost_raw <- tryCatch(
    TOSTER::tsum_TOST(
      m1 = mean(comp, na.rm = TRUE), sd1 = sd(comp, na.rm = TRUE), n1 = n1,
      m2 = mean(ref,  na.rm = TRUE), sd2 = sd(ref,  na.rm = TRUE), n2 = n2,
      low_eqbound = -raw_bound, high_eqbound = raw_bound,
      eqbound_type = "raw", alpha = 0.05
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(tost_raw)) return(NULL)

  tost_lower_p <- tost_raw$TOST$p.value[2]
  tost_upper_p <- tost_raw$TOST$p.value[3]
  tost_p_max_raw <- max(tost_lower_p, tost_upper_p, na.rm = TRUE)

  tibble(
    dv = dv,
    dv_label = unname(dv_labels[dv]),
    pooled_sd = pooled_sd,
    raw_bound_pos = raw_bound,
    raw_diff = mean(comp, na.rm = TRUE) - mean(ref, na.rm = TRUE),
    tost_p_max_raw = tost_p_max_raw,
    equivalent_raw = tost_p_max_raw < 0.05
  )
})

# Cross-check against SMD result
tost_compare <- tost_results %>%
  select(dv, dv_label, equivalent_smd = equivalent, tost_p_max_smd = tost_p_max) %>%
  left_join(tost_raw_results %>%
              select(dv, equivalent_raw, tost_p_max_raw, raw_bound_pos),
            by = "dv") %>%
  mutate(agree = equivalent_smd == equivalent_raw)

tost_compare %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)),
         equivalent_smd = ifelse(equivalent_smd, "✓", "✗"),
         equivalent_raw = ifelse(equivalent_raw, "✓", "✗"),
         agree = ifelse(agree, "agree", "DISAGREE")) %>%
  kbl(caption = "TOST robustness: SMD bounds (preregistered) vs. raw bounds (TOSTER author's recommendation)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE)

n_disagree <- sum(!tost_compare$agree, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(glue::glue(
  "\nSMD-bound and raw-bound TOST procedures agree on {nrow(tost_compare) - n_disagree} of ",
  "{nrow(tost_compare)} DVs. ",
  "{if (n_disagree == 0) 'The SMD bias warning does not affect any of our equivalence conclusions; the preregistered SMD-bound test is reported as primary.' else paste0('Disagreement on: ', paste(tost_compare %>% filter(!agree) %>% pull(dv_label), collapse = '; '), '. We retain the preregistered SMD-bound result as primary but flag these DVs for transparency.')}\n"
))

save_table(tost_raw_results, "04d_tost_equivalence_raw_bounds")
save_table(tost_compare, "04e_tost_smd_vs_raw_agreement")
```

# 7. Bot Verbosity: Confound-Competition Sensitivity (Prereg §8.3)

## 7.1 Compute per-participant verbosity from chat_log

```{r verbosity-compute}
library(jsonlite)

compute_bot_verbosity <- function(chat_log_str) {
  if (is.na(chat_log_str) || chat_log_str == "") return(NA_real_)
  log <- tryCatch(fromJSON(chat_log_str, simplifyVector = FALSE),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(log)) return(NA_real_)
  bot_turns <- keep(log, ~.x$role == "assistant")
  if (length(bot_turns) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  # Use OpenRouter-reported completion_tokens where available
  toks <- map_dbl(bot_turns, function(t) {
    if (!is.null(t$usage) && !is.null(t$usage$completion_tokens)) {
      as.numeric(t$usage$completion_tokens)
    } else {
      # Fallback: char count / 4 as a proxy
      nchar(t$content) / 4
    }
  })
  mean(toks, na.rm = TRUE)
}

compute_bot_chars <- function(chat_log_str) {
  if (is.na(chat_log_str) || chat_log_str == "") return(NA_real_)
  log <- tryCatch(fromJSON(chat_log_str, simplifyVector = FALSE),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(log)) return(NA_real_)
  bot_turns <- keep(log, ~.x$role == "assistant")
  if (length(bot_turns) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  mean(map_dbl(bot_turns, ~nchar(.x$content)), na.rm = TRUE)
}

compute_user_chars <- function(chat_log_str) {
  if (is.na(chat_log_str) || chat_log_str == "") return(NA_real_)
  log <- tryCatch(fromJSON(chat_log_str, simplifyVector = FALSE),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(log)) return(NA_real_)
  user_turns <- keep(log, ~.x$role == "user")
  if (length(user_turns) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  mean(map_dbl(user_turns, ~nchar(.x$content)), na.rm = TRUE)
}

compute_user_total_chars <- function(chat_log_str) {
  if (is.na(chat_log_str) || chat_log_str == "") return(NA_real_)
  log <- tryCatch(fromJSON(chat_log_str, simplifyVector = FALSE),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(log)) return(NA_real_)
  user_turns <- keep(log, ~.x$role == "user")
  if (length(user_turns) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  sum(map_dbl(user_turns, ~nchar(.x$content)), na.rm = TRUE)
}

df_primary <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(
    bot_tokens_per_turn = map_dbl(chat_log, compute_bot_verbosity),
    bot_chars_per_turn = map_dbl(chat_log, compute_bot_chars),
    user_chars_per_turn = map_dbl(chat_log, compute_user_chars),
    user_total_chars = map_dbl(chat_log, compute_user_total_chars)
  )
df_sensitivity <- df_sensitivity %>%
  mutate(
    bot_tokens_per_turn = map_dbl(chat_log, compute_bot_verbosity),
    bot_chars_per_turn = map_dbl(chat_log, compute_bot_chars),
    user_chars_per_turn = map_dbl(chat_log, compute_user_chars),
    user_total_chars = map_dbl(chat_log, compute_user_total_chars)
  )
```

## 7.2 Descriptive verbosity comparison (Prereg §8.3)

```{r verbosity-compare}
verbosity_test <- welch_full(df_primary, "bot_tokens_per_turn")
verbosity_test %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 2))) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Bot verbosity (mean completion tokens per turn) by condition") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

# Bot character verbosity for comparison

  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 2))) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Bot characters per turn by condition (verification)") %>%
```

## 7.3 Verbosity-adjusted DV regressions (Prereg §8.3)

Each of the ten confirmatory *t*-tests is repeated as a linear regression of the DV on Condition (LowA = 0, HighA = 1) and mean bot completion tokens per turn (centered). The condition coefficient and verbosity coefficient are both reported.

<!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): document Type II partial eta² and the exact unadjusted comparison -->
Partial η² for each term is computed from Type II sums of squares, so the condition η² is adjusted for verbosity (and vice versa). Each adjusted model is compared with the unadjusted model `DV ~ Condition` fit to the same rows: `raw_b` / `raw_eta2` are the unadjusted condition coefficient and partial η², and `pct_change_b` / `pct_change_eta` are the exact percentage changes. `interpretation_v` is a descriptive summary of these numbers and does not apply a robustness criterion. <!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (C1) -->

```{r verbosity-adjusted}
# Center verbosity for interpretability
df_primary <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(bot_tokens_c = bot_tokens_per_turn - mean(bot_tokens_per_turn, na.rm = TRUE),
         cond_dummy = ifelse(condition_label == "HighA", 1L, 0L))

# FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): helper — pull the partial eta² for one term from an effectsize table.
# (effectsize names the column Eta2_partial for >1 term but Eta2 for a single-term model.)  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
pull_eta2 <- function(es_tbl, term) {                                          # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
  es_tbl <- as.data.frame(es_tbl)                                                # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
  col <- intersect(c("Eta2_partial", "Eta2"), names(es_tbl))[1]                 # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
  stopifnot(!is.na(col), sum(es_tbl$Parameter == term) == 1)                    # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): row must exist exactly once
  es_tbl[[col]][es_tbl$Parameter == term]                                        # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
}                                                                                # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
# FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): exact partial eta² from Type II SS, used as an independent cross-check
pe2_from_anova <- function(aov2, term) {                                         # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
  ss <- aov2[["Sum Sq"]]; names(ss) <- rownames(aov2)                            # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
  unname(ss[term] / (ss[term] + ss["Residuals"]))                                # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
}                                                                                # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)

verbosity_adjusted_results <- map_dfr(confirmatory_dvs, function(dv) {
  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): fit adjusted and unadjusted models on the SAME rows so the change is comparable
  d_m <- df_primary %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[dv]]), !is.na(cond_dummy), !is.na(bot_tokens_c))  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
  f <- as.formula(glue("{dv} ~ cond_dummy + bot_tokens_c"))
  m <- lm(f, data = d_m)                                                         # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): data = d_m (same rows as before; no NA dropped differently)
  m0 <- lm(as.formula(glue("{dv} ~ cond_dummy")), data = d_m)                    # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): unadjusted model, same rows
  coefs <- broom::tidy(m, conf.int = TRUE)
  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): Type I eta² (condition entered first) is NOT adjusted for verbosity.
  # Use Type II SS so each term's partial eta² is adjusted for the other term.  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
  aov2_m  <- car::Anova(m,  type = 2)                                            # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
  aov2_m0 <- car::Anova(m0, type = 2)                                            # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
  ph  <- effectsize::eta_squared(aov2_m,  partial = TRUE, ci = 0.95)             # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): Type II partial eta²
  ph0 <- effectsize::eta_squared(aov2_m0, partial = TRUE, ci = 0.95)             # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): unadjusted model eta²

  # Get condition row
  c_row <- coefs %>% filter(term == "cond_dummy")
  v_row <- coefs %>% filter(term == "bot_tokens_c")
  c_eta <- pull_eta2(ph, "cond_dummy")                                           # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): explicit cond_dummy row, Type II
  v_eta <- pull_eta2(ph, "bot_tokens_c")                                         # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): explicit bot_tokens_c row, Type II
  r_eta <- pull_eta2(ph0, "cond_dummy")                                          # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): exact raw partial eta² (m0)
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(c_eta, pe2_from_anova(aov2_m,  "cond_dummy"))),    # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): cross-check vs SS
            isTRUE(all.equal(r_eta, pe2_from_anova(aov2_m0, "cond_dummy"))))     # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): cross-check vs SS

  # Compare to raw effect from results_primary
  raw_d <- results_primary %>% filter(dv == !!dv) %>% pull(d)
  raw_p <- results_primary %>% filter(dv == !!dv) %>% pull(p)

  tibble(
    dv = dv,
    dv_label = dv_labels[dv],
    raw_d = raw_d,
    raw_p = raw_p,
    cond_b = c_row$estimate, cond_se = c_row$std.error,
    cond_t = c_row$statistic, cond_p = c_row$p.value,
    cond_lo = c_row$conf.low, cond_hi = c_row$conf.high,
    cond_eta2 = c_eta,
    verb_b = v_row$estimate, verb_p = v_row$p.value, verb_eta2 = v_eta,
    R2 = summary(m)$r.squared,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
    n_model  = nrow(d_m),                                                        # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): added — rows in both models
    raw_b    = unname(coef(m0)["cond_dummy"]),                                   # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): added — unadjusted condition b
    raw_eta2 = r_eta                                                             # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): added — exact unadjusted partial eta²
  )
})

verbosity_adjusted_results <- verbosity_adjusted_results %>%
  mutate(
    q_bh_adj = p.adjust(cond_p, method = "BH")
  )

# FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): changes are now computed EXACTLY against the unadjusted model (m0).
# raw_eta2_approx (d-to-eta² conversion) is retained unchanged for backward compatibility only.  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
# interpretation_v is now a purely descriptive, computed label; it takes no position on a  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
# robustness criterion.  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
verbosity_adjusted_results <- verbosity_adjusted_results %>%
  mutate(
    raw_eta2_approx = (raw_d^2) / (raw_d^2 + 4),  # approximate conversion for two groups (kept; not used below)  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
    pct_change_b   = (cond_b - raw_b) / raw_b * 100,                             # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): added — % change in condition b
    pct_change_eta = (cond_eta2 - raw_eta2) / raw_eta2 * 100,                    # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): exact (was vs. d-converted approx)
    interpretation_v = sprintf(                                                  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): descriptive label, no robustness rule
      "%s (raw p = %s); adjusted b changes by %+.1f%% (%.3f -> %.3f); adjusted partial eta2 %.4f -> %.4f (%+.1f%%); adjusted p = %s; adjusted q_BH = %s",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
      ifelse(raw_p < 0.05, "Raw effect p < .05", "Raw effect p >= .05"),         # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
      fmt_p(raw_p), pct_change_b, raw_b, cond_b, raw_eta2, cond_eta2, pct_change_eta,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
      fmt_p(cond_p), fmt_p(q_bh_adj))                                            # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)
  )  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1)

verbosity_adjusted_results %>%
  select(dv_label, raw_d, raw_p, raw_b, cond_b, pct_change_b, cond_se, cond_p, q_bh_adj,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): show raw_b / pct_change_b
         raw_eta2, cond_eta2, pct_change_eta, verb_b, verb_p, verb_eta2, R2, interpretation_v) %>%  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C1): show raw_eta2 / pct_change_eta
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)),
         raw_p = fmt_p(raw_p), cond_p = fmt_p(cond_p), q_bh_adj = fmt_p(q_bh_adj),
         verb_p = fmt_p(verb_p)) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Verbosity-adjusted DV regressions (primary sample)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE)

save_table(verbosity_adjusted_results, "05_verbosity_adjusted")
```

## 7.4 Side-by-side comparison plot

```{r verbosity-side-by-side, fig.height=6}
side_data <- bind_rows(
  results_primary %>%
    select(dv_label, d, d_lo, d_hi) %>%
    mutate(model = "Raw (Welch t)"),
  verbosity_adjusted_results %>%
    transmute(dv_label,
              # Convert adjusted eta² back to d-scale roughly for comparison
              d = sign(cond_b) * 2 * sqrt(cond_eta2 / (1 - cond_eta2)),
              d_lo = NA, d_hi = NA,
              model = "Verbosity-adjusted (partial eta-sq)")
)

p_side <- side_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = d, y = reorder(dv_label, d), color = model, shape = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = d_lo, xmax = d_hi), height = 0.2,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.4), na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Raw (Welch t)" = "#1E5BA8",
                                 "Verbosity-adjusted (partial eta-sq)" = "#B45F06")) +
  labs(title = "Effect of condition on each DV: raw vs. verbosity-adjusted",
       subtitle = "Adjusted estimates use partial eta-sq converted to d-scale (CIs not shown for adjusted)",
       x = "Effect size (Hedges' g or d-equivalent)", y = NULL,
       color = NULL, shape = NULL)
p_side
save_fig(p_side, "03_raw_vs_verbosity_adjusted", w = 9, h = 6)
```

# 9. Confirmatory Directional Hypothesis: Legal Expertise Moderator (Prereg RQ-E8, §9.1)

## 9.1 Build the legal-expertise composite

```{r legal-expertise}
# d_training is a multi-select character; check actual format
df_primary %>% count(d_training) %>% head(10)

# Heuristic: d_training contains substring "law" or codes indicating legal training
# Examine and adjust based on actual values
df_primary <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(
    legal_training_law = str_detect(tolower(as.character(d_training)), "law"),
    legal_training_law = replace_na(legal_training_law, FALSE),
    jury_yes = (d_jury == 1) & !is.na(d_jury),
    legal_knowledge_z = scale(d_legal_knowledge)[, 1],
    legal_expertise = legal_knowledge_z +
                      2 * as.numeric(legal_training_law) +
                      0.5 * as.numeric(jury_yes)
  )

df_primary %>%
  summarize(
    `N with law training` = sum(legal_training_law, na.rm = TRUE),
    `N with jury experience` = sum(jury_yes, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Legal-knowledge mean (raw)` = mean(d_legal_knowledge, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Legal-knowledge SD (raw)` = sd(d_legal_knowledge, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Composite mean` = mean(legal_expertise, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Composite SD` = sd(legal_expertise, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Composite min` = min(legal_expertise, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Composite max` = max(legal_expertise, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything()) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Legal-expertise composite descriptives", booktabs = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## 9.2 H-Legal: One-tailed test of the interaction

```{r h-legal-test}
df_primary <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(legal_expertise_z = scale(legal_expertise)[, 1],
         cond_centered = ifelse(condition_label == "HighA", 0.5, -0.5))

m_legal <- lm(liab_corp ~ cond_centered * legal_expertise_z, data = df_primary)
m_legal_summary <- summary(m_legal)
print(m_legal_summary)

interaction_coef <- broom::tidy(m_legal, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term == "cond_centered:legal_expertise_z")
interaction_coef

# Convert two-tailed p to one-tailed (sign matters for directional prediction)
# FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a): prereg RQ-E8 predicts ATTENUATION (a smaller absolute condition effect at higher
# FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)  legal expertise), not a sign. This notebook's one-tailed test assumes a NEGATIVE
# FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)  interaction, which corresponds to attenuation only when the condition main effect is positive.
two_tailed_p <- interaction_coef$p.value
one_tailed_p <- if (interaction_coef$estimate < 0) {
  two_tailed_p / 2
} else {
  1 - two_tailed_p / 2
}

# FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a): live attenuation quantities from the fitted model (narrative only; one_tailed_p and
# FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)  the 'supported' rule are unchanged). Condition simple slope at z = legal_expertise_z:
# FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)  b_cond + z * b_int. |slope(+1)| < |slope(-1)| is the RQ-E8 attenuation criterion.
hl_terms  <- c("cond_centered", "cond_centered:legal_expertise_z")                         # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
hl_b_main <- unname(coef(m_legal)[hl_terms[1]])   # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a): condition effect at mean legal expertise (z = 0)
hl_b_int  <- unname(coef(m_legal)[hl_terms[2]])                                            # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
hl_V      <- vcov(m_legal)[hl_terms, hl_terms]                                              # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
hl_tcrit  <- qt(0.975, df.residual(m_legal))                                                # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
hl_slope  <- function(z) {                                                                  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
  est <- hl_b_main + z * hl_b_int                                                           # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
  se  <- sqrt(hl_V[1, 1] + z^2 * hl_V[2, 2] + 2 * z * hl_V[1, 2])                           # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
  c(est = est, lo = est - hl_tcrit * se, hi = est + hl_tcrit * se)                          # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
}                                                                                           # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
hl_s_lo <- hl_slope(-1); hl_s_hi <- hl_slope(1)                                             # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
hl_attenuated <- abs(hl_s_hi[["est"]]) < abs(hl_s_lo[["est"]])                              # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
hl_main_sign  <- if (hl_b_main > 0) "positive" else if (hl_b_main < 0) "negative" else "zero"  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
hl_int_sign   <- if (interaction_coef$estimate > 0) "positive" else if (interaction_coef$estimate < 0) "negative" else "zero"  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
hl_int_ci_txt <- sprintf("b = %.3f, 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f]", interaction_coef$estimate,      # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
                         interaction_coef$conf.low, interaction_coef$conf.high)             # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
hl_slopes_txt <- sprintf(paste0("Condition simple slope at -1 SD of legal_expertise_z = %.3f [95%% CI %.3f, %.3f]; ",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
                                "at +1 SD = %.3f [95%% CI %.3f, %.3f]"),                     # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
                         hl_s_lo[["est"]], hl_s_lo[["lo"]], hl_s_lo[["hi"]],               # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
                         hl_s_hi[["est"]], hl_s_hi[["lo"]], hl_s_hi[["hi"]])               # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
hl_attn_txt <- sprintf(paste0("|slope(+1 SD)| = %.3f %s |slope(-1 SD)| = %.3f, so the RQ-E8 attenuation ",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
                              "criterion (|slope(+1 SD)| < |slope(-1 SD)|, point estimates) is %s"),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
                       abs(hl_s_hi[["est"]]), if (hl_attenuated) "<" else ">=",             # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
                       abs(hl_s_lo[["est"]]), if (hl_attenuated) "met" else "not met")      # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
hl_onetail_txt <- sprintf(paste0("The one-tailed test assumes a negative interaction, which corresponds to ",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
                                 "attenuation only when the condition main effect is positive; here the ",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
                                 "condition main effect (at mean legal expertise) is %s (b = %.3f)"),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
                          hl_main_sign, hl_b_main)                                          # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)

cat(glue(
  "\nH-Legal directional test:\n",
  "  Interaction β = {round(interaction_coef$estimate, 4)}\n",
  "  SE = {round(interaction_coef$std.error, 4)}\n",
  "  t = {round(interaction_coef$statistic, 3)}\n",
  "  Two-tailed p = {round(two_tailed_p, 4)}\n",
  "  One-tailed p (H-Legal) = {round(one_tailed_p, 4)}\n",
  "  Interaction observed: {hl_int_sign} ({hl_int_ci_txt})\n",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a): was "Direction predicted: NEGATIVE"
  "  One-tailed test: assumes a NEGATIVE interaction (this notebook's operationalization of RQ-E8)\n",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
  "  Condition main effect (at mean legal expertise): b = {sprintf('%.3f', hl_b_main)} ({hl_main_sign});\n",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
  "    a negative interaction corresponds to attenuation only when this main effect is positive\n",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
  "  {hl_slopes_txt}\n",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
  "  {hl_attn_txt}\n",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
  "  H-Legal supported (p < .05, one-tailed): {ifelse(one_tailed_p < 0.05 & interaction_coef$estimate < 0, 'YES', 'NO')}\n"
))

save_table(broom::tidy(m_legal, conf.int = TRUE), "07_h_legal_regression")
```

```{r simple-slopes}
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(ss$slopes$Est.[ss_z == -1]), unname(hl_s_lo[["est"]]))),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5a)
```

## 9.4 Tertile-split robustness check

```{r legal-tertile}
df_primary <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(legal_tertile = cut(legal_expertise,
                             breaks = quantile(legal_expertise,
                                                probs = c(0, 1/3, 2/3, 1),
                                                na.rm = TRUE),
                             labels = c("Low", "Mid", "High"),
                             include.lowest = TRUE))

m_tertile <- lm(liab_corp ~ condition_label * legal_tertile, data = df_primary)
anova_tertile <- car::Anova(m_tertile, type = 3)
print(anova_tertile)

# Simple effects of condition within each tertile
em <- emmeans::emmeans(m_tertile, ~ condition_label | legal_tertile)
contrasts_tertile <- pairs(em)
print(contrasts_tertile)

save_table(broom::tidy(anova_tertile), "08_legal_tertile_anova")
```

## 9.5 H-Legal extensions to other liability DVs

```{r h-legal-extensions}
extension_dvs <- c("liab_chat", "liab_user", "liab_harm")
extensions <- map_dfr(extension_dvs, function(dv) {
  f <- as.formula(glue("{dv} ~ cond_centered * legal_expertise_z"))
  m <- lm(f, data = df_primary)
  coef <- broom::tidy(m, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term == "cond_centered:legal_expertise_z") %>%
    mutate(dv = dv, dv_label = dv_labels[dv])
  coef
})

extensions %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 4)),
         p.value = fmt_p(p.value)) %>%
  select(dv_label, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, conf.low, conf.high) %>%
  kbl(caption = "H-Legal extensions to other liability DVs (exploratory)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

save_table(extensions, "09_h_legal_extensions")
```

# 10. Internal Consistency Reliability (Prereg §8.5)

```{r reliability}
reliability_results <- tibble(
  Scale = character(),
  N_items = integer(),
  alpha = numeric(),
  alpha_lo = numeric(),
  alpha_hi = numeric(),
  omega = numeric()
)

scale_items <- list(
  PSR_total = paste0("psr_", 1:12),
  PSR_connection = paste0("psr_", 1:4),
  PSR_desire = paste0("psr_", 5:8),
  PSR_caring = paste0("psr_", 9:12),
  EC = paste0("ec_", 1:5),
  Trust = paste0("tr_", 1:4),
  Experience_Taking = paste0("et_", 1:8),
  Moral_Agency = paste0("ma_", 1:8),
  Moral_Patiency = paste0("mp_", 1:8),
  Liability_Corporate = paste0("liab_", 1:5),
  Liability_Chatbot = paste0("liab_", 6:8),
  Liability_User = paste0("liab_", 9:10),
  Liability_Harm = paste0("liab_", 11:12),
  GAAIS_Positive = c(paste0("gaais_", 1:9), "gaais_10_r"),  # placeholder
  GAAIS_Negative = c(paste0("gaais_", 11:18), "gaais_19_r", "gaais_20_r"),
  PHQ4 = paste0("phq4_", 1:4)
)

# Prepare reverse-coded GAAIS items
df_rel <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(gaais_10_r = 6 - gaais_10,
         gaais_19_r = 6 - gaais_19,
         gaais_20_r = 6 - gaais_20)

reliability_results <- map_dfr(names(scale_items), function(scale_name) {
  items <- scale_items[[scale_name]]
  available <- intersect(items, names(df_rel))
  if (length(available) < 2) {
    return(tibble(Scale = scale_name, N_items = length(available),
                  alpha = NA, alpha_lo = NA, alpha_hi = NA, omega = NA))
  }

  X <- df_rel[, available, drop = FALSE]
  X <- X[complete.cases(X), , drop = FALSE]

  set.seed(42)  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-R1): reseed before each stochastic psych::alpha bootstrap
  alpha_obj <- tryCatch(psych::alpha(X, check.keys = FALSE,
                                      n.iter = 1000, warnings = FALSE),
                        error = function(e) NULL)
  alpha_val <- if (!is.null(alpha_obj)) alpha_obj$total$raw_alpha else NA_real_
  alpha_ci <- if (!is.null(alpha_obj) && !is.null(alpha_obj$boot.ci)) {
    alpha_obj$boot.ci
  } else c(NA, NA, NA)

  omega_val <- tryCatch({
    if (length(available) >= 3) {
      o <- psych::omega(X, nfactors = 1, plot = FALSE, warnings = FALSE)
      o$omega.tot
    } else NA_real_
  }, error = function(e) NA_real_)

  tibble(
    Scale = scale_name,
    N_items = length(available),
    alpha = alpha_val,
    alpha_lo = alpha_ci[1],
    alpha_hi = alpha_ci[3],
    omega = omega_val
  )
})

reliability_results <- reliability_results %>%
  mutate(flag = case_when(
    N_items < 2 ~ "—",
    alpha < 0.60 ~ "⚠ <0.60 (treat as exploratory)",
    alpha < 0.70 ~ "Borderline",
    TRUE ~ "Acceptable"
  ))

reliability_results %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3))) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Internal consistency reliability: Cronbach's α (with bootstrap 95% CI) and McDonald's ω") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

# Live exploratory-flag list for the manuscript
exploratory_scales <- reliability_results %>%
  filter(!is.na(alpha), alpha < 0.60) %>% pull(Scale)
borderline_scales <- reliability_results %>%
  filter(!is.na(alpha), alpha >= 0.60, alpha < 0.70) %>% pull(Scale)

if (length(exploratory_scales) > 0 || length(borderline_scales) > 0) {
  cat("\n--- Reliability flags for manuscript ---\n")
  if (length(exploratory_scales) > 0) {
    cat(glue::glue("Below 0.60 (treat as exploratory; flag in manuscript): ",
                   "{paste(exploratory_scales, collapse = ', ')}\n"))
  }
  if (length(borderline_scales) > 0) {
    cat(glue::glue("Borderline (0.60-0.70; report with caveat): ",
                   "{paste(borderline_scales, collapse = ', ')}\n"))
  }
}

save_table(reliability_results, "10_reliability")
```

# 11. Item-Level Analyses with Forest Plots (Exploratory item-level supplement; see Prereg RQ-E3)

For each multi-item DV composite and subscale, item-level Welch's *t*-tests with BH-FDR applied within scale.

## 11.1 Run item-level tests for all DVs

```{r item-level-tests}
item_specs <- list(
  PSR_full = paste0("psr_", 1:12),
  PSR_connection = paste0("psr_", 1:4),
  PSR_desire = paste0("psr_", 5:8),
  PSR_caring = paste0("psr_", 9:12),
  EC = paste0("ec_", 1:5),
  Trust = paste0("tr_", 1:4),
  Experience_Taking = paste0("et_", 1:8),
  Moral_Agency = paste0("ma_", 1:8),
  Moral_Patiency = paste0("mp_", 1:8),
  Liability_Corporate = paste0("liab_", 1:5),
  Liability_Chatbot = paste0("liab_", 6:8),
  Liability_User = paste0("liab_", 9:10),
  Liability_Harm = paste0("liab_", 11:12)
)

item_level <- imap_dfr(item_specs, function(items, scale_name) {
  map_dfr(items, ~welch_full(df_primary, .x)) %>%
    mutate(scale = scale_name) %>%
    mutate(q_bh_within = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"))
})

item_level <- item_level %>%
  mutate(
    sig_within_scale = q_bh_within < 0.05,
    direction = ifelse(d > 0, "HighA > LowA", "LowA > HighA")
  )

# DIF descriptive: SD of effect sizes within each scale
dif_summary <- item_level %>%
  group_by(scale) %>%
  summarize(n_items = n(),
            mean_d = mean(d, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_d = sd(d, na.rm = TRUE),
            min_d = min(d, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_d = max(d, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_sig = sum(sig_within_scale, na.rm = TRUE))

dif_summary %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3))) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Differential item functioning summary: within-scale SD of item-level effect sizes") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

save_table(item_level, "11_item_level")
save_table(dif_summary, "11_dif_summary")
```

## 11.2 Forest plots per scale

```{r forest-per-scale, fig.height=10, fig.width=10}
make_forest <- function(scale_name, item_data) {
  d <- item_data %>%
    filter(scale == scale_name) %>%
    mutate(item = factor(dv, levels = dv[order(d)]))

  ggplot(d, aes(x = d, y = item)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey50") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-0.5, 0.5), linetype = "dotted", color = "grey80") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = d_lo, xmax = d_hi), height = 0.2, color = "grey30") +
    geom_point(aes(fill = sig_within_scale), shape = 21, size = 3, color = "black") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#1A7E3A", "FALSE" = "white"),
                      name = "Sig (within-scale FDR)",
                      labels = c("FALSE" = "No", "TRUE" = "Yes")) +
    labs(title = scale_name, x = "Hedges' g", y = NULL) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"))
}

# Generate forest plots for the larger scales
forest_plots <- map(names(item_specs), make_forest, item_data = item_level)
names(forest_plots) <- names(item_specs)

# Compose into a grid
top_row <- forest_plots$PSR_full +
  (forest_plots$Experience_Taking) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1))

mind_row <- forest_plots$Moral_Agency + forest_plots$Moral_Patiency

liab_row <- forest_plots$Liability_Corporate +
  (forest_plots$Liability_Chatbot / forest_plots$Liability_Harm) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.5, 1))

ec_trust_row <- forest_plots$EC + forest_plots$Trust + forest_plots$Liability_User

# Save individual forest plots
for (sc in names(forest_plots)) {
  save_fig(forest_plots[[sc]], glue("forest_{sc}"), w = 6, h = 4)
}

# Display a few key ones
print(forest_plots$PSR_full)
print(forest_plots$Moral_Patiency)
print(forest_plots$Liability_Corporate)
```

## 11.4 Confirmatory findings — pointer to synthesis

A consolidated synthesis of all confirmatory and exploratory findings (Findings #1–#8) is provided at the end of the notebook (§14), after all relevant models have been fit. Placing the synthesis after §12 (Exploratory) and §13 (Sample Description) lets it pull live values from M1, M3, m_tipi_ma, and the moderator battery, instead of fallback "not yet fit" placeholders.

The high-level pattern, quantified live (details in §14): `r sum(results_primary$confirmed[results_primary$dv %in% c("psr_total", "ec_total", "trust_total")])` of the three bonding measures (PSR, EC, Trust) and `r sum(results_primary$confirmed[results_primary$dv %in% c("liab_corp", "liab_chat", "liab_user", "liab_harm")])` of the four liability measures meet the confirmation rule (*q*~BH~ < .05 and BF₁₀ ≥ 3). The mediation, mind-perception, personality-matching, and free-speech-moderator analyses to follow address whether any pathway from condition to liability emerges below the level of the primary main effect. <!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (C5): replaced hard-coded "reliably moves ... does not move" takeaway with live counts -->

# 12. Exploratory Analyses (Prereg §9)

## 12.1 Individual difference moderators (Prereg §9.1)

For brevity, the interaction tests are summarized in a single results table. Significant interactions get follow-up simple-slopes plots.

```{r moderators}
# FIX 2026-09-30 (C2): recode non-substantive codes to NA before they enter the battery.
# Codes verified against experiment/experiment.js (Study 1 & 2 identical):  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
#   d_politics:    1 = Very liberal ... 7 = Very conservative; 8 = "Prefer not to say / Not applicable"  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
#   d_religiosity: 1 = Not at all ... 5 = Extremely religious/spiritual; 6 = "Prefer not to say"  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
#   d_age: free numeric entry (HTML min 18 / max 100 not enforced); impossible values (e.g., 1821) -> NA,  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
#          using the same 16-100 rule as d_age_clean in §13 (which is created later in the notebook).  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
df_primary <- df_primary %>%  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
  mutate(  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
    d_age_mod         = ifelse(d_age > 100 | d_age < 16, NA_real_, d_age),  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2): impossible ages -> NA
    d_politics_mod    = na_if(d_politics, 8),                                # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2): 8 = prefer not to say / N.A. -> NA
    d_religiosity_mod = na_if(d_religiosity, 6)                              # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2): 6 = prefer not to say -> NA
  )  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
cat(glue::glue(                                                              # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2): report recodes
  "Moderator recodes: d_age -> NA for {sum(is.na(df_primary$d_age_mod) & !is.na(df_primary$d_age))} case(s); ",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
  "d_politics code 8 -> NA for {sum(df_primary$d_politics == 8, na.rm = TRUE)} case(s); ",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
  "d_religiosity code 6 -> NA for {sum(df_primary$d_religiosity == 6, na.rm = TRUE)} case(s).\n"))  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)

moderator_set <- list(
  PHQ4_total = "phq4_total",
  PHQ4_anxiety = "phq4_anx",
  PHQ4_depression = "phq4_dep",
  TIPI_self_agree = "tipi_self_agree",
  Chatbot_experience = "d_chatbot_experience",
  GAAIS_positive = "gaais_pos",
  GAAIS_negative = "gaais_neg",
  Politics = "d_politics_mod",        # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2): was d_politics (code 8 scored as a scale point)
  Religiosity = "d_religiosity_mod",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2): was d_religiosity (code 6 scored as a scale point)
  FreeSpeech = NULL,  # composite below
  Age = "d_age_mod"                   # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2): was raw d_age (contained 1821)
)

# Build free-speech composite (mean of the two items)
df_primary <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(free_speech_avg = (d_free_speech_1 + d_free_speech_2) / 2)
moderator_set$FreeSpeech <- "free_speech_avg"

run_moderator <- function(dv, mod_var, mod_name) {
  if (is.null(mod_var) || !mod_var %in% names(df_primary)) {                 # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2): never drop a moderator silently
    stop(glue("run_moderator(): moderator column '{mod_var}' ({mod_name}) not found in df_primary"))  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
  }  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
  m_data <- df_primary %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[dv]]), !is.na(.data[[mod_var]])) %>%
    mutate(mod_z = scale(.data[[mod_var]])[, 1],
           cond = ifelse(condition_label == "HighA", 0.5, -0.5))
  if (nrow(m_data) < 20) {                                                   # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2): warn instead of silent drop
    msg <- glue("run_moderator(): {mod_name} x {dv} skipped (n = {nrow(m_data)} < 20)")  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
    cat("[C2 WARNING]", msg, "\n"); warning(msg)                                          # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2): visible despite warning = FALSE
    return(NULL)  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
  }  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
  f <- as.formula(glue("{dv} ~ cond * mod_z"))
  m <- lm(f, data = m_data)
  coef <- broom::tidy(m, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term == "cond:mod_z") %>%
    transmute(dv = dv, dv_label = dv_labels[dv],
              moderator = mod_name,
              interaction_b = estimate, interaction_se = std.error,
              interaction_p = p.value,
              ci_lo = conf.low, ci_hi = conf.high,
              n = nrow(m_data))
  coef
}

moderator_results <- expand.grid(dv = confirmatory_dvs,
                                  mod_name = names(moderator_set),
                                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  pmap_dfr(function(dv, mod_name) {
    run_moderator(dv, moderator_set[[mod_name]], mod_name)
  })

# FIX 2026-09-30 (C2): every moderator x DV test must be present; report n used per moderator
missing_tests <- nrow(expand.grid(confirmatory_dvs, names(moderator_set))) - nrow(moderator_results)  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
if (missing_tests > 0) {                                                                              # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
  cat("[C2 WARNING]", missing_tests, "moderator x DV test(s) were not run\n")                          # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2): visible
  warning(glue("{missing_tests} moderator x DV test(s) were not run"))                                 # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
} else cat("[C2 check] all", nrow(moderator_results), "moderator x DV tests were run.\n")             # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
print(moderator_results %>% group_by(moderator) %>%  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)
        summarize(n_min = min(n), n_max = max(n), .groups = "drop"))                                  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C2)

# Highlight notable interactions
moderator_results <- moderator_results %>%
  mutate(notable = interaction_p < 0.05)

moderator_results %>%
  arrange(interaction_p) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)),
         interaction_p = fmt_p(interaction_p)) %>%
  head(25) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Top 25 condition × moderator interactions (sorted by p)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE)

save_table(moderator_results, "13_moderators")
```

### 12.1.1 Follow-up on theoretically-notable moderator clusters

<!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (C5): replaced hard-coded claims ("opposite-signed effects across DVs"; "TIPI-Self Agreeableness × Moral Agency is the strongest interaction in the table") with a neutral description; the characterization is computed live in the chunks below. -->
Two moderator clusters are followed up beyond the omnibus exploratory listing. What each one shows in the final sample is computed from the live moderator table in the chunks below, not asserted here. All moderator tests are exploratory and uncorrected. <!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (C5) -->

**Free-speech attitudes.** Flagged as a candidate cluster during data collection (a possible reading in which participants higher in free-speech endorsement treat bot warmth as engineered persuasion, which would predict lower bonding *and* higher corporate-responsibility attributions). The chunk below reports whether any free-speech × condition interaction reaches p < .05 and whether the signs split between bonding and liability DVs. <!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (C5) -->

**Personality matching (TIPI-Self Agreeableness × condition).** Participant agreeableness is the self-report analogue of the manipulated trait. We plot its interaction with condition on Moral Agency and, separately, on whichever DV has the strongest TIPI-Self Agreeableness × condition interaction in the live moderator table. The Moral Agency follow-up was selected at an interim look during data collection, when it was the strongest TIPI-Self × condition interaction; it is not preregistered (Prereg §9.1 lists TIPI-Self Agreeableness as a moderator of every DV but names no Moral Agency follow-up). It is kept for continuity with earlier versions of this notebook and should be read as post hoc. <!-- FIX 2026-09-30 (C5): replaced unsupported "originally planned follow-up" provenance with the documented interim-look selection -->

```{r moderator-followup-freespeech}
# Free-speech moderator pattern across DVs
fs_pattern <- moderator_results %>%
  filter(moderator == "FreeSpeech") %>%
  arrange(interaction_p) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)),
         interaction_p = fmt_p(interaction_p)) %>%
  select(dv_label, interaction_b, interaction_se, interaction_p, ci_lo, ci_hi, n)

fs_pattern %>%
  kbl(caption = "Free-Speech × Condition interactions across all 10 DVs") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

# Data-driven characterization: pull live values, decide what to say based on what's actually there
fs_raw <- moderator_results %>% filter(moderator == "FreeSpeech")

bonding_dvs_set <- c("psr_total", "ec_total", "trust_total")
liab_dvs_set    <- c("liab_corp", "liab_chat", "liab_user", "liab_harm")

fs_bond <- fs_raw %>% filter(dv %in% bonding_dvs_set)
fs_liab <- fs_raw %>% filter(dv %in% liab_dvs_set)

n_sig_any  <- sum(fs_raw$interaction_p < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
min_p      <- min(fs_raw$interaction_p, na.rm = TRUE)
n_total    <- nrow(fs_raw)

# Sign pattern (only meaningful if the magnitudes are not trivially small)
median_bond_b <- median(fs_bond$interaction_b, na.rm = TRUE)
median_liab_b <- median(fs_liab$interaction_b, na.rm = TRUE)
opposite_signs <- (median_bond_b * median_liab_b) < 0

cat("\n--- Free-speech moderator (data-driven characterization) ---\n")
cat(glue::glue(
  "Significant interactions (p < .05): {n_sig_any} of {n_total} DVs. ",
  "Smallest p across DVs: {sprintf('%.3f', min_p)}.\n"
))

if (n_sig_any == 0) {
  cat("No free-speech × condition interaction reaches conventional significance ",
      "in the final analytic sample. ",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C5): removed stale "Earlier knits at smaller N" history claim
      "We do not pursue a substantive interpretation here.\n",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (C5)
      sep = "")
} else if (opposite_signs) {
  cat(glue::glue(
    "The free-speech moderator shows opposite-signed median interactions on ",
    "bonding DVs (median b = {round(median_bond_b, 3)}) vs. liability DVs ",
    "(median b = {round(median_liab_b, 3)}). With {n_sig_any}/{n_total} ",
    "individual interactions reaching p < .05 (uncorrected), ",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5c)
    "we report the pattern descriptively.\n"  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5c): was "suggestive but not robustly supported" (fixed evaluative label)
  ))
} else {
  cat(glue::glue(
    "The free-speech moderator shows {n_sig_any}/{n_total} significant ",
    "individual interactions (smallest p = {sprintf('%.3f', min_p)}). ",
    "The median interactions on bonding DVs (b = {round(median_bond_b, 3)}) and liability DVs ",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5c)
    "(b = {round(median_liab_b, 3)}) have the same sign; we report results descriptively without ",  # FIX 2026-09-30 (R4-C5c): was "does not consolidate into a coherent split"
    "substantive interpretation.\n"
  ))
}

save_table(fs_pattern, "13b_freespeech_moderator_pattern")
```
